question.problem: Let $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7 \\ k\end{aligned}]$  belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$

current_example.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154149/assets/42b0fc416a10396d3e43a9cff5bf7b6e3412401212eede8ddb040156f94d94d7.svg) be a linear transformation. Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154149/assets/fd8843c332a325328b999cba3e764b9525ebca6cbed5b473cac0efacd510dc8b.svg) belongs to $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T}).$
current_example.worked_solution:
The vector $\mathbf{v}$ belongs to $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})$ if there exists a vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154149/assets/8af9a20e7ccc841981f90b4857f3003d2e5898f958d13a8d7757f0b8d8d21fbf.svg) such that $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u}) = \mathbf{v}.$ 

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ -x+y \\ 2y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ k \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y=4 \\ -x+y=k \\ 2y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $y=4,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y & =4 \\ x+4 & =4 \\ x & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=0$ and $y=4$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+y & =k \\ 0+4 & =k \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\mathbf{v}\in\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})$ when $k=4.$
